hypothesis: session.cold_open_10mib launch_to_ready_ms (~21-25s p50 on a 10MiB session) is dominated by redundant full-content parsing on the daemon load path: the window walk pays an Envelope pass plus a Value+tagged-flatten Content double-buffer per retained line, SessionFile::open_windowed re-parses every retained row as SessionEntry through another flatten Content buffer, and the retained-ids index re-parses every raw row a second time.
approach: Three focused changes on the load path (lane lane/hillclimb-session-open, base 7152746b): (1) pa-types/src/session.rs - FileEntry::deserialize gains a single-pass fast path for `message` rows (the bulk of a large session): it builds the entry field-by-field from the already-parsed JSON map (user/assistant/toolResult roles, thinking/text/toolCall/textSignature/image blocks) with one clone per payload into its final owner, instead of the tagged mirror's Value->Content->struct double buffering; any shape the fast path does not unambiguously recognize falls through to the original KnownFileEntry mirror, so acceptance and every rest catch-all stay identical. (2) pa-daemon/src/session_store.rs - SessionEntry deserialization becomes a single-pass map visitor (envelope fields straight from the stream, catch-all collected in source order) instead of the derived flatten that buffered every row through a second content generation. (3) open_windowed collects the retained ids from the parse the loop already runs, deleting a second full parse of every retained row. Parity tests added: fast-path-vs-mirror corpus (message_fast_path_matches_tagged_mirror), round-trips, single-pass visitor shape test.
parity_notes: No session byte changes: every JSONL line still parses and replays (thinking blocks, tool calls, tool results, custom rows, unknown kinds degrade to Unknown verbatim); the fast path is strictly conservative (falls back to the unmodified tagged mirror on ANY ambiguity), the single-pass SessionEntry visitor differs from the derive only by being last-wins on duplicate envelope keys (derive rejected them; more accepting, closer to TS JSON.parse - documented in code and flagged by adversarial pre-review, fixed in commit 4f3d4c018); retained_ids is the same set, branch() semantics unchanged; Serialize paths untouched; no wire/protocol/tool/system-prompt changes; no tests weakened or deleted (tests added). Adversarial pre-review verdict: CLEAN on parity.

measurements.method: parallel-sandboxes (cross-VM pair; ITERATION evidence only - NOT PR evidence per the fleet-wide A/A methodology addendum)
measurements.honest_interpretation: This cross-VM pair is CONFOUNDED and backs no conclusion. The apparent deltas sit inside the measured cross-VM 5x A/A factor: within the SAME pair, the candidate VM shows -6.6%/-5.8% on the 10MiB suites while showing +366.7%/+391.3% on compare.cold_start/compare.warm_start (pure process starts, no session load) in the same window - a self-contradictory pattern only a VM/host factor can produce (host oversubscription, cand VM hit hardest in the later suites). Additionally, cand cold_open trials 3-4 (44.5s/46.9s vs 22.8-24.9s for its other trials) coincide with this worker's own probe execs (duration_s 275.8/288.1, probe sends 107) - probe-perturbed. The dead-end verdict therefore rests on the open-audit decomposition, not this pair: the JSONL parse (windowed reverse scan + full parse of the 10MiB fixture) costs ~97ms of the ~21-25s ready path; the real cost is the retained-transcript resume pipeline, superlinear in retained message count (135 msgs=0.26s, 1406=0.33s, 7259=21.3s). The ~2.5x reduction in per-line parse tree-generations is real but lands on a ~100ms slice.

validity.notes: All 50 trials (5 suites x 5 trials x 2 VMs) err=False and sentinel/echo/erased valid. Per-VM calibration (3x python3 busy-loop, median): base VM 1.0736s, cand VM 1.0553s (1.7% divergence - the VMs calibrate equal at rest). BUT during the suite window the cand VM's process-start metrics ran ~5x base (cold_start 2.7s vs 0.57s p50) - transient host oversubscription, matching perf-binary-size's decisive A/A finding (same binary, 0.31s vs 1.6s cold-start across VMs). Cross-VM pairs are iteration evidence only; PR evidence requires same-vm-sequential ABBA, which was NOT run (discarded before PR per orchestrator decision - no mechanism gain to justify it).

decision: DISCARDED as a PR. Orchestrator verdict (open-audit decomposition): parse-side optimization is negligible vs the replay pipeline - the JSONL parse costs ~97ms of the ~21-25s cold-open ready time, while the retained-transcript resume pipeline is superlinear in retained message count (135=0.26s, 1406=0.33s, 7259=21.3s). The pair-1 cross-VM comparison cannot contradict this: its apparent deltas (cold_open +0.7% with cand outliers, scroll -6.6%, memory -5.8%) sit within the measured cross-VM 5x VM factor (proven in-pair by the same-binary 5x cold_start/warm_start divergence), and cand cold_open trials 3-4 were probe-perturbed. The mechanism itself (single-pass parses, 3 commits on lane/hillclimb-session-open) is parity-clean and gate-clean and stays available for a future axis where parse cost actually dominates (e.g. pure file-open paths, traces, exports, foreign-file scans). The lane will not be PR'd; worker re-scoped to the retained-transcript replay pipeline (daemon-vs-TUI split) per the new top-priority axis.
